citation.title: Topology Optimization with Text-Guided Stylization
citation.authors: Shengze Zhong, Parinya Punpongsanon, Daisuke Iwai, and Kosuke Sato

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: In three 2D benchmarks, the neural method's compliance was close to SIMP: bridge 181.08 versus 181.06, MBB 40.80 versus 39.48, and L-bracket 177.23 versus 169.80.
claim.key_phrase: similar topology optimization performance to SIMP
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: No classical-method speed-up factor is stated or derivable from the reported comparison.
claim.alternatives: Section 4.4 reports 58.66 seconds for 100 iterations at 256×256; Section 5 says convergence speed and quality are worse than traditional explicit methods, without a measured head-to-head speed comparison.

baseline.implementation: 165-line Python SIMP code attributed to Niels Aage and Villads Egede Johansen (Section 4.1)
baseline.solver: Finite element analysis; solver type not stated
baseline.ml_time: not stated for Section 4.1 comparison; Section 4.4 reports 58.66 s for 100 iterations at 256×256
baseline.data_generation_cost: not stated; no offline training dataset for the method is described
baseline.quality_gap: Compliance pairs for SIMP and neural method: bridge 181.06/181.08, MBB 39.48/40.80, L-bracket 169.80/177.23; volumes are also compared (Section 4.1).

R1.evidence: Section 4.1 compares design quality; no speed comparison is the primary outcome.

R2.evidence: Section 4.1 identifies a Python SIMP implementation but does not establish an R2 efficiency criterion.

R3.evidence: Sections 3–4 optimize the neural representation for each problem; no offline model training cost is claimed.

R4.evidence: Section 4.1 evaluates compliance and volume for compared designs, but no rate of infeasible or failed outputs is reported.

reporting.n_test_cases: Three compliance comparison tasks (bridge, MBB, L-bracket), with additional stylized 2D and 3D examples (Sections 4.1–4.4).

notes: Section 4.4 reports an average iteration time for a single 256×256 bridge example; this is not a timing comparison against SIMP. The article notes that its penalty method may miss target volume constraints and that pure topology optimization quality and convergence can lag explicit methods (Section 5).
